sources.source: Crime in England and Wales: Police Force Area data tables, year ending March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The current official dataset was released on 23 July 2026 and provides police-recorded-crime figures by Police Force Area and Community Safety Partnership area. ONS states that estimates may be revised when further data arrive or methods and systems change.
sources.quality_effect: Adds current subnational recorded-crime crosschecks while retaining police-recording, boundary, denominator, revision, transient-population and no-parcel-downscaling guards.

sources.source: Crime in England and Wales: Appendix tables, year ending March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The 23 July 2026 edition supplies the year-ending-March-2026 appendix tables for Crime Survey for England and Wales and police-recorded crime, including offence-level detail on violence, fraud and anti-social behaviour.
sources.quality_effect: Adds offence-level national trend crosschecks while separating survey and administrative sources and retaining sampling, telephone-survey-period, recording and revision guards.

sources.verified_fact: The 23 July 2026 Q4 release covers January to March 2026. It reports a 10.5% quarterly increase in child-abuse-flagged referrals, an 8.0% increase in rape-flagged charges and an overall CPS court caseload above 210,000.
sources.quality_effect: Adds prosecution-flow context while preserving the CPS warning that the data are operational management information, provisional, system-derived and not official crime or court statistics.

sources.source: Prison population: monthly prison figures 2026, June bulletin
sources.verified_fact: The official transparency page was updated on 13 July 2026 with the June 2026 monthly prison-population bulletin and provides monthly population breakdown data for the prison estate.
sources.quality_effect: Adds current custody-capacity context while retaining snapshot-date, establishment, sex, age, nationality, sentence-status and monthly-flow-versus-stock guards.

sources.source: Prison population: weekly estate figures 2026, 20 July bulletin
sources.verified_fact: The official weekly estate summary was updated on 20 July 2026 with the prison-population bulletin for that date, providing the latest point-in-time estate summary.
sources.quality_effect: Adds near-current capacity monitoring while retaining point-in-time, operational-capacity, transfer, temporary-closure, daily-volatility and non-incident guards.

sources.source: Exploring the feasibility of a survey measuring child abuse: May 2026
sources.verified_fact: The 6 May 2026 ONS research update assesses whether school and online survey approaches can measure the current extent and nature of child abuse. It states that administrative data capture only cases reported to or identified by authorities and support organisations.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a hidden-harm measurement guard while retaining feasibility-study, consent, disclosure, coverage, safeguarding-protocol and no-prevalence-estimate limits.

sources.source: Stability measures for children looked after in England: 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official 30 April 2026 release measures placement, school and professional-support stability for children looked after on 31 March 2025, using the SSDA903 return from local authorities and school-census data.
sources.quality_effect: Adds safeguarding-continuity context while retaining stock-date, eligibility, multiple-placement, school-enrolment, professional-change and local-authority-recording guards.

sources.source: Children looked after in England including adoption: 2024 to 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited 20 November 2025 release provides national and local-authority information for looked-after children in the year ending 31 March 2025, based on SSDA903 returns collected from all local authorities.
sources.quality_effect: Adds care-population context while separating children, episodes, starts, ceasing care, legal status, placement type and adoption outcomes; it is not abuse prevalence or parcel risk.

sources.source: Legal aid statistics quarterly: January to March 2026
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and Legal Aid Agency
sources.verified_fact: The accredited 25 June 2026 publication covers criminal and civil legal aid, family mediation, legal-aid providers, central-funds payments, inquests, client diversity and provider contracts for January to March 2026.
sources.quality_effect: Adds access-to-justice context while retaining application-versus-grant, matter-start-versus-client, eligibility, provider-capacity, payment-timing and policy-change guards.

sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 147,814 deaths referred to coroners in 2025 and 622 deaths in state detention reported to coroners. It notes that the statutory Medical Examiner system introduced in September 2024 changed referral volumes and case mix.
sources.quality_effect: Adds death-investigation context with referral-versus-registered-death, occurrence-versus-conclusion-year, state-detention definition, medical-examiner-system and local-resource guards.

sources.source: Family Court Statistics Quarterly: January to March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 71,259 new family-court cases in January to March 2026, 3% more than a year earlier, including increases in private-law, public-law and domestic-violence case starts. Care and supervision cases took an average of 37 weeks to disposal.
sources.quality_effect: Adds family-justice and protection-order context while retaining case-versus-person, application-versus-order, case-type, repeat-application, timeliness and court-processing guards.

sources.source: How many people are detained under immigration powers in the UK?, year ending March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The official-statistics-in-development release reports 22,586 entries into immigration detention in the year ending March 2026 and 1,955 people detained at 31 March 2026. One individual can enter or leave detention more than once and therefore be counted multiple times.
sources.quality_effect: Adds detention-system context while retaining occurrence-versus-person, end-quarter snapshot, detention-estate-versus-prison, nationality, legal-status and developing-statistics guards.

quality_guards: AREA_LEVEL_PROXY only; no parcel measurement claim.
Police Force Area and Community Safety Partnership data use administrative geographies and police recording systems.
CSEW, TCSEW and police-recorded crime are separate statistical series.
CPS figures are provisional operational management information, not official crime or court statistics.
Monthly and weekly prison population figures are point-in-time capacity measures rather than safety incidents.
Child-abuse survey research is a feasibility study and does not provide a prevalence estimate.
Looked-after-children stability, stock, episodes, placement and legal status are distinct units.
Legal-aid applications, grants, matters, clients, contracts and payments must not be conflated.
Coroner referrals and conclusions can relate to different occurrence years and were affected by the statutory Medical Examiner system.
Family-court cases and remedies do not measure unique people or underlying harm prevalence.
Immigration-detention entries can count the same individual more than once; end-quarter figures are snapshots.
The uploaded 046 note remains non-canonical without matching task, heartbeat, claim and receipt evidence.
